title: [V1][Spec Decode] Optimize N-gram matching with Numba (#13365)

experiments.name: ngram_match_overhead
experiments.workload: 5000 synthetic context sequences (len 200-800, vocab 32000), n-gram n=3, k=10; ~50% seeded with a plantable match. Cumulative NgramProposer.propose() time over the full 5000-seq pass; 5 repeats (gold warmed up once untimed to exclude JIT compile).
experiments.note: PREFERRED approach: imported the standalone vllm/v1/spec_decode/ngram_proposer.py module directly from each mounted source tree (self-contained, only numpy/numba/typing deps) and timed .propose(). base=pure-python KMP loop; gold=numba @jit(nopython=True) kernels. runs = per-repeat cumulative seconds; speedup_x = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios. numba not baked in image -> installed at runtime via pip (numba 0.68.1, arm64 wheel); worked.

environment: docker vllm-cpu-bench:21222 (python:3.12-slim + CPU torch arm64 wheel, numpy 2.5.4), colima arm64 Mac; identical image for both arms, only vllm/ source tree differs. numba NOT baked into image -> installed at runtime with `pip install numba` (numba 0.68.1, arm64 wheel) for the gold arm; base arm is pure-python and needs no numba. gold arm warmed up once (untimed) to exclude numba JIT compile from the steady-state timing.

title: [Perf] Optimize detokenizer python logic (#32975)

experiments.name: detokenize
experiments.workload: 200 seqs x 2000 tokens; isolated SlowIncrementalDetokenizer per-token output-count check (slice vs tracked), 7 repeats
experiments.note: approach=fallback (self-contained, both arms in ONE process on the same CPU, no cross-container noise). Reproduces the exact changed inner logic: base recomputes len(self.token_ids[self.prompt_len:]) per token (slice alloc), gold uses num_output_tokens()==len(token_ids)-prompt_len. speedup_x = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios. NOTE: the real full detokenizer path was ALSO driven (PYTHONPATH=/src, real gpt2 tokenizer via transformers, real SlowIncrementalDetokenizer.update() loop, batched updates, long prompt); there the native tokenizer decode (~5us/tok) dominates and the slice removal is below run-to-run noise (real base ~5.36 us/tok vs gold ~6.39 us/tok, i.e. no measurable end-to-end gain). The isolated fallback below matches the PR's own reported methodology of timing the detokenizer PYTHON logic in isolation.

environment: docker vllm-cpu-bench:32975 (python:3.12-slim + CPU torch + transformers + gguf), PYTHONPATH=/src with per-arm vllm source tree mounted ro; colima arm64 Mac (aarch64), py 3.12.16; identical image for both arms, only vllm/ source differs

title: [Perf] Optimize Python Slice for Structured Output using `islice` instead of [:] (#33593)

experiments.name: membership_present
experiments.workload: SIZE=100_000, end-token at 10%% in; `tok not in input_ids[:-1]` vs `tok not in islice(input_ids,0,len-1)`; INNER=200 calls/block, 18 paired samples, best-of + mean±sd
experiments.note: Real PR hot path (reasoning parser extract_content_ids). Marker present early -> islice short-circuits + copies nothing; list[:-1] copies all N first. Gold wins.

experiments.name: membership_absent
experiments.workload: SIZE=100_000, end-token absent; same two idioms; INNER=200, 18 paired samples
experiments.note: HONEST TRADEOFF: when the token is absent both scan all N, but list[:-1] is a C-level memcpy + C-level `in`, while islice yields through the Python iterator protocol per element. Gold is SLOWER here. Net PR win depends on how often reasoning has already ended (present case dominates in practice).

experiments.note: base = recompute inspect.getsource+sha256 each call; gold = functools.cache wrapped (cold miss then hits); speedup = mean of per-repeat base/gold ratios

title: [Core] Use array to speedup padding (#6779)

experiments.name: make_tensor_with_pad
experiments.workload: SamplingTensors padding-input prep + 2x make_tensor_with_pad (prompt+output), input_len=1024, batch_size=2048, pad=vocab_size(32000), dtype=int64, device=cpu; 1 warmup, 5 timed repeats
experiments.note: FINDING: PR #6779 does NOT touch make_tensor_with_pad; that fn is BYTE-IDENTICAL at base and gold (already the np.full/make_ndarray_with_pad array path). The real change is the INPUT fed to it inside SamplingTensors.from_sampling_metadata/from_lists: base builds List[List[int]] via list(seq_data.prompt_token_ids) (tuple->list copies); gold passes seq_data.prompt_token_ids_array (array('l')) directly, SequenceData now storing tokens as array. Benchmark loads the REAL unmodified make_tensor_with_pad from each mounted tree by source (vllm import chain needs the absent _custom_ops C ext) and replicates the exact per-arm prep path. speedup_x = mean of per-run base/gold ratios.

environment: docker vllm-cpu-bench:21222 (CPU torch 2.15.0+cpu, numpy 2.5.4), colima arm64 Mac; identical image for both arms, only vllm/ source tree differs; real make_tensor_with_pad loaded by source from each mounted tree
